note: Foundation or organisation level rules, applied when a repository itself says nothing. Owners are GitHub owner names (case-insensitive). stance: forbid | disclose | oversight | allow | silent; silent means the body publishes no AI rule and only its cla/dco facts are used. rule is the sentence printed as the reason when the stance is inherited. Placeholders in disclosure_line: {agent} {model} {tool}.

orgs.name: Apache Software Foundation
orgs.rule: generative tooling may be used for an ASF contribution when the contributor holds the rights to the output, and the contribution has to record which tool produced it, by convention a Generated-by: trailer
orgs.cla: ICLA only for committers; not needed for a pull request
orgs.note: Applies to every ASF project unless the project publishes something stricter (Airflow, Arrow, Kvrocks, DataFusion do). Enforcement is per project.

orgs.name: Cloud Native Computing Foundation
orgs.rule: the foundation publishes no rule about AI-assisted contributions; every commit needs a DCO sign-off from the human contributor
orgs.note: Every CNCF project requires a DCO sign-off on each commit. The person submitting signs; an agent must not add Signed-off-by.

orgs.name: GNOME
orgs.rule: github.com/GNOME is a read-only mirror of gitlab.gnome.org and pull requests opened there are not accepted; several GNOME projects also reject generative AI contributions outright
orgs.note: Work on gitlab.gnome.org instead. Several GNOME projects (libadwaita, gedit, Amberol, GIMP) reject generative AI contributions outright; check the project CONTRIBUTING.md on GitLab.

orgs.name: Linux kernel and projects using the kernel Assisted-by convention
orgs.rule: a coding assistant may be used and the commit has to say so with an Assisted-by: trailer; the Signed-off-by line stays the human contributor's alone
orgs.note: docs.kernel.org/process/coding-assistants: the kernel itself writes the trailer as `Assisted-by: LLM [tool1] [tool2]` (tools = analysis tools such as coccinelle); Zephyr, Fedora, Rocky Linux, Mesa and OpenInfra use `Assisted-by: <Agent>:<Model> [tools]`. In all of them AI agents must not add Signed-off-by; only the human contributor certifies the DCO. torvalds/linux and openstack on GitHub are mirrors that do not take pull requests.

orgs.name: Python Software Foundation / CPython
orgs.rule: AI-assisted work is accepted from a contributor who understands and can defend every line of it, and saying that a tool helped is welcome rather than required
orgs.disclosure_line: This change was prepared with the help of {tool}; I reviewed and tested it myself.
orgs.cla: PSF Contributor Agreement (click-through, checked by a bot on the pull request)
orgs.note: CPython asks contributors to say when AI was used and to understand every line; the PSF CLA is required before a pull request can be merged.

orgs.name: Eclipse Foundation
orgs.rule: the foundation publishes no rule about AI-assisted contributions; every commit needs an Eclipse Contributor Agreement and a DCO sign-off from the human contributor
orgs.cla: Eclipse Contributor Agreement (ECA) signed with the committer's Eclipse account; commits must use the same email
orgs.note: The ECA includes the DCO; each commit needs Signed-off-by from the human contributor.
